messages:
From: Aayla Rahman <aayla.rahman@cardiotech.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: MAP + cost model for inference POC

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the demo last week — team was impressed with the throughput. Were trying to pull together a mutual action plan for a 6-8 week POC and need a cost model to validate internal approval. Can you share a MAP that includes: tokens/$ assumptions, expected batching and caching behavior, and an evaluation plan (milestones + pass/fail criteria)?

Attached is a small sample of our traffic (inference-sample-traffic.json). Key constraints: ~200k requests/day, many short sessions (avg 40 tokens/request), spike to 5k rps for 10s during peak. Latency SLO target: p95 < 300ms.

Target close: decision by end of July if the POC economics check out. Appreciate a breakdown of per-token economics for hosted vs dedicated and any quick wins (prefetch, KV cache) we should enable in the POC.

Thanks,
Aayla Rahman
Head of Platform, CardioTech
--
CardioTech | https://cardiotech.com

From: priyom.das@redwood.com
To: aayla.rahman@cardiotech.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: MAP + cost model for inference POC

Aayla, thanks — sending an initial MAP draft and a token-econ worksheet for your review (CardioTech-MAP-v2.xlsx attached). High-level notes:

- Baseline tokens/$ numbers: hosted model (gpt-like 13B variant) ~ $0.0025 per 1k tokens served; dedicated (reserved) can drop ~25% depending on commit and batching.
- Batching assumptions we used: typical request batch size 8 (continuous batching with 50ms wait window) until p95 latency budget.
- Caching: we recommend prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts in sessions; expect 10-30% token reduction for the sample traffic depending on prompt reuse.

Action items: can you confirm (A) whether the 200k/day is steady-state or front-loaded into a few customers, and (B) your expected session length distribution? Ive put placeholders in the worksheet so we can swap numbers quickly.

Well also include an evaluation plan section with checkpoints (week 1 ingest & baseline, week 3 batching/caching tuning, week 6 performance sign-off).

If it works, Ill loop in Karthik for a short tech session to validate the latency profile and batching windows.

Best,
Priyom Das

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: aayla.rahman@cardiotech.com
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 09:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: MAP + cost model for inference POC

Replying all with a few tech clarifications and recommended eval checks we should include in the MAP:

- Traffic shape: if the spike is short (10s bursts), continuous batching should still help but we should cap batching window to 30-50ms to protect p95. For long bursts we can rely on burst capacity in Dedicated.
- KV cache: recommend a session-level LRU with 10k entries for the POC; metric to watch is cache hit rate and token reduction delta by cohort. Expect ~15% token savings if callers reuse prompts.
- Token accounting: split tokens into prompt tokens, completion tokens, and system tokens. Worksheet currently uses avg 40 tokens/request (prompt+completion) — we should ask CardioTech to split those numbers; completion-heavy flows change economics more.
- Eval plan: add gating criteria — (a) p95 < 300ms at target load, (b) unit cost <= $0.0035/request (based on their target ACV), (c) no functional regressions on 50 eval prompts.

Ill prepare a short runbook for week-3 tuning (batch sizes, cache policy, quantization knob) and drop it into the MAP. Karthik, can you sanity-check the 25% drop estimate for reserved capacity?

Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Internal note: see inference-sample-traffic.json attached to prior external mail for session-level breakdown.

From: Aayla Rahman <aayla.rahman@cardiotech.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: devops@cardiotech.com
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: MAP + cost model for inference POC

Thanks — this looks good. A few quick clarifications to help you finalize the numbers:

- The 200k/day is an average across our platform; roughly 60% comes from interactive sessions (session length avg 6 requests), 40% from system batch jobs (single request, larger prompt).
- For POC we can allow 3% error budget on latency for non-critical internal tooling, but product-facing paths must meet p95 < 300ms.
- Wed like to see an itemized delta between (1) hosted with default batching, (2) hosted with aggressive batching (50ms), and (3) dedicated with reserved commit + batching.

Also: can Redwood provide an expected monthly cost range (low/median/high) in the MAP for the sample traffic with caching on/off? That will be the deciding input for procurement.

Regards,
Aayla

From: priyom.das@redwood.com

Aayla — attaching the final econ worksheet (cardiotech-final-econ-worksheet.xlsx) and an updated MAP with evaluation milestones. Summary highlights:

- Estimated monthly spend (sample traffic, median usage): Hosted-default batching = ~$6,200/mo; Hosted-aggressive batching (50ms) = ~$4,700/mo; Dedicated (3-month reserve + batching) = ~$3,500/mo (post-commit). All numbers assume a 15% token reduction from KV caching for interactive cohorts.
- Latency: with 50ms batching window p95 remains under 300ms in our small-scale test; we recommend week-1 smoke to validate in CardioTech env and week-3 tuning for cache policies.
- MAP milestones: Week 0: contract & infra access, Week 1: baseline ingest & smoke, Week 3: batching/caching tuning, Week 5: quantization/throughput test, Week 7: final sign-off.
